assessment: experimental_only; all styles and sizes sampled, not every encoded glyph manually proofread

methods.bitmap: Pixels decoded directly from exported SJPB files using family.bitmap_reader.BitmapFont; never rebuilt from geometry; composing with BitmapFont.mask honors exported horizontal and vertical bearings.
methods.ttf: Final TTF files rendered through installed Pillow/FreeType, no geometry regeneration; native monochrome fontmode=1, nearest-neighbor enlargement. This is separate from the exported SJPB bitmap review.
methods.pixel_policy: All 60 delivered proof PNGs are native 1-bit mode with only 0/255 pixels; enlargement uses nearest neighbor.
methods.reference_discipline: Only project-original glyph renders and ASCII identifiers; no external reference-font glyph images are distributed.

findings.title: Distinct shapes collapse into the same small bitmap
observations: 已/巳 are pixel-identical at 16 px in Gothic, Italian, Subscript and Superscript.
己/已/巳 are pixel-identical at 18 px in Subscript and Superscript.
煮/煮 remain pixel-identical at 32 px in Subscript and Superscript.
The separate exhaustive CJK audit finds additional groups outside this visual sample.
findings.action: Introduce explicitly reviewed optical bitmap designs or minimum-size guidance for affected styles. Preserve encoded identities; do not merely change coverage labels.

findings.title: Dense Kanji counters and component gaps close
observations: At 16/18 px, many sampled dense glyphs merge into dark regions in weighted styles and especially the two reduced styles.
32 px recovers more structure but does not clear every counter: Italian and reduced-style 爨/麤/櫜 and weighted 鬮 remain crowded.
This is not evidence that the earlier high-resolution geometry corrections were undone.
findings.action: Tune component spacing, stroke thickness and per-size optical geometry; proofread each affected dense form. Use the Singleline 32 px proof as an additional view, not as typography approval.

findings.title: Reduced styles over-compress enclosures and already-small numerals
observations: Circled two-digit numerals are crowded at 16/18 px, most severely in Subscript/Superscript.
Applying a reduced whole-font style to encoded superscript/subscript numerals makes a second reduction; several 16 px forms become only a few pixels high.
Negative discs retain cutout pixels in the viewed samples; remaining issues are legibility and crowding.
findings.action: Design size-specific counters/numerals and document minimum useful sizes. Do not use reduced whole-font styles for dense text or already-reduced Unicode numerals without proofing.

findings.title: Small pictogram signs and internal details merge
observations: Key teeth, snowflake arms, building signs and cart details merge or lose clarity at small sizes, especially reduced styles.
32 px is visibly clearer for most viewed pictograms, but small building signs can still thicken markedly in weighted styles.
findings.action: Provide optically simplified small-size pictograms with deliberately preserved semantic signs; review the affected PUA codepoints and their documented Unicode aliases.

findings.title: Three inherited pairs remain identical
observations: 剝/剥, 塡/填 and 頬/頰 have identical baseline-aligned pixels and advances in all 32 strikes.
These source-equivalent inherited pairs predate this size expansion.
findings.action: Continue explicit disclosure. Separate original designs are required if distinctions are a project requirement.

findings.title: Two spacing dots vanished in reduced 16 px strikes
findings.original_detection: Exhaustive audit reported blank glyphs in Subscript16 and Superscript16; these glyphs were outside the original 172-character visual sample.
findings.bounded_fix: Build owner widened only the two authored spacing-dot segments from 0.7 to 1.6 grid units; no generic blank-glyph fallback.
findings.recheck: The actual repaired bytes were visually inspected in all 32 strikes. Every case is nonblank. Original 5504 reviewed glyph/style/size pixel hashes and metrics are unchanged.

boundaries: Full repertoire structural and collision tests are a separate machine audit, not a manual visual approval.
Earlier VISUAL-QA.md documents 190 sampled glyphs; overlap exists and those counts must not be added without deduplication.
Expanded Kanji remain composition/design drafts. Regional, overlay, enclosure and deep-composition risk flags remain relevant.
No platform-wide shaping test, reader recognition study or Japanese typographic certification was performed.
No geometry, glyph source, generator, canonical asset, or font file was edited by this review.

spacing_dot_fix_recheck.review_note: The 64 new SJPB dot cases and 96 TTF dot cases were viewed in ten added proof sheets. Previously reviewed cells were not claimed as newly manually re-inspected: 5504 existing SJPB pixel/metric records and all 50 previous proof-image hashes match exactly.
